newsitem.title: FRANCE: Alcatel steps up campaign for Thomson-CSF.
newsitem.headline: Alcatel steps up campaign for Thomson-CSF.

text.p: Electronics and engineering group Alcatel Alsthom on Wednesday stepped up its campaign to win in the privatisation bidding for defence electronics company Thomson-CSF.
The government is selling its 58 percent stake in Thomson-CSF as part of a defence industry restructuring, which has major implications for a consolidation around Europe.
Alcatel officials argued that a sale of the stake to Alcatel and its joint bidder Dassault Industries, instead of to rival Lagardere, would be in the best interests of Thomson-CSF and France.

They said that an exclusive deal signed between Lagardere's Matra unit and Daimler-Benz Aerospace (Dasa) as well as a deal between Matra and British Aerospace could weaken France's role in the Airbus consortium and the Arianespace rocket group as it would hurt state-owned aerospace group Aerospatiale.

Alcatel executives believe Lagardere would not keep Thomson-CSF intact, a charge Lagardere last week denied. They also said their offer would bring valuable assets to Thomson-CSF and make it a global player in many fields.
The French government has said it will announce the outcome of the bidding before the end of June but after the parliamentary election being held on May 25 and June 1.

Alcatel officials said that they would strengthen ties with General Electric Co Plc and Thomson-CSF and perhaps bring together both companies' naval electronics activities in Thomson's Signaal unit of the Netherlands.

Alcatel would also negotiate with Dasa over joint ventures. "We hope that the exclusive deal between Matra and Dasa is not irreversible," Christian Pinon, managing director of Alcatel's Radio, Space and Defence division, told journalists.

"We do not need 2.7 billion francs ($480 million) from BAe, we do not need to agree to the break-up of Thomson-CSF. Our offer is based on the financial capacity of Alcatel and Dassault and we do not need any financial engineering by banks nor any prior deals with BAe and Dasa," Pinon said, referring to Lagardere's financing from banks and accords with BAe and Dasa.
BAe is putting up 300 million sterling to help finance the bid from Lagardere, which has also arranged bank loans and is issuing a convertable bond to help its funding.

But despite their arguments in favour of their offer, Alcatel officials were unable to explain why they expected the government to change its mind -- the centre-right government of Alain Juppe late last year said Lagardere was the preferred bidder and had earlier apparently dismissed Thomson chairman Alain Gomez because he wanted a closer alliance with GEC.
"With a new government, new chances," an official said.
Pinon said that the country's independent Privatisation Commission was currently studying both offers, even before the next government would be able to look at the documents.
"If the offers vary a lot, it will all be played on price," he said, declining to state Alcatel's offer price.

A company official noted that recent U.S. defence deals had been conducted at a price 1.8 times annual sales. This would give Thomson-CSF a total value of 64.8 billion francs, or some 37.5 billion for the state's 58-percent stake.

Pinon underlined the synergies between Thomson-CSF and Alcatel, noting the two had a common history and, when both state-owned, agreed in 1983 that Alcatel would concentrate on civil while Thomson-CSF focused on military communications.
Both Thomson-CSF and Alcatel have products in their line-up which stem from former European units of ITT.

Alcatel's defence activities centre on military communications, including rapid deployment infrastructure for front-line units. The group is also active in command and control centres as well as in battle simulation.

The division had 1996 sales of 10.65 billion francs, with new orders at 12.54 billion francs. Almost all of the division will be transferred to Thomson-CSF if Alcatel wins. Some stand-alone units will be transferred immediately, others will first have to be broken out of existing Alcatel units.
Dassault Industrie's Dassault Electronique, which will also be transferred to Thomson-CSF, will bring in radar, missile guidance and jamming technologies.
"It's a marriage with benefits for both," Pinon said.
($ = 5.640 French Francs)
